This Court passed a detailed order on 14/7/2023 which is reproduced as under:-
This is petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking following reliefs and interim reliefs:-
(a) Quashing of charges framed under Section 228 of Cr.P.C against the petitioner on 17/02/2017 in Session Trial No.699/2016 by the Special Judge Shri A.K. Paliwal,
ADJ(I).
(Certified copy of charge framed is enclosed at Annexure -E, Page No.40-44).

(b) Issue direction for inquiry and for dismissal from service of Respondent No.1, 2 and 3 for conducting malicious prosecution against the petitioner and these Public Servants are also dangerous to society for conducting prosecution against the innocent people and willfully acting dishonestly against the procedure of law even after having aware about the facts and making false statement in the judicial proceedings.

( d ) Issue direction to the Bar counsel of Madhya Pradesh for cancellation of License to practice in Courts of Madhya Pradesh by the respondent No.4 for hiding the truths from the Court and cheating is own client.
INTERIM ORDER/WRIT PRAYED.
(a) That, respondent No.1, 2, 3, and 4 be directed to submit Affidavit in reply with supporting records/documents in terms of Section 207 of Cr.P.C for prosecuting the petitioner under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 201 and 120B of IPC:

(i) Copy of First Information Report (FIR) Under Section 154 of Cr.P.C in which petitioner is being named for committing Cognizable Offence under Section 420, 424,
467, 468, 471, 201 and 120B of IPC.

(ii) Copy of Statement of Witnesses recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C for the purpose of cross examination of witness during the criminal trial proceedings which directly concerns to Petitioner for committing the cognizable offence under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 201 and 120 B of IPC.

(iii) Copy of Statement of Witnesses recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C for the purpose of cross examination of witness during the trial proceedings which directly concerns to Petitioner for committing the cognizable offence under Section 420, 467,
468, 471, 201 and 120 B of IPC which was also been submitted before the Trial Court on 19/1/2017 by on order dated 9/1/2017.
(Copy of order at Annexure - F, Page No.45-46)

(iv) Copy of Documentary Evidence collected during the course of investigation and was forwarded to Magistrate under Section 173 (5) of Cr.P.C and are directly concerns to petitioner and the prosecution is relying upon those documents to prosecute petitioner under Section 420, 424, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of IPC.
( v ) Respondent No.3 Shri Nirmal Kumar Mandloi, Special Public Prosecutor as submitted the written statement on 23/01/2023 before the Trial Court that accused was been provided complete charge-sheet alongwith CD, documents and statement of witnesses recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C respondent No.3 be directed to furnish all the documents as stated by him in written submission (copy of written submission is enclosed as Annexure - G, Page No.47)
2.In regard to relief claimed in 7(a) for quashing of the charges under Section 228 of Cr.P.C against the petitioner on 17/2/2017 in Sessions Trial No.699/2017 by the Special Judge
, it is not in dispute that the order of framing of charge was challenged by the petitioner through his Advocate before this Court and the said case was dismissed.
At present the petitioner is not in position to give the details of the case numb er of that case.
In view of the aforesaid that the challenge to the order of framing of charge has already been unsuccessful, the said relief cannot be granted in the writ petition.
3. The next relief 7 (b) is being sought a direction for enquiry and for dismissal from service of respondent Nos.1, 2, 3 for conducting malicious prosecution against the petitioner.

It is submitted that the applicant filed application for malicious prosecution which was dismissed by the Trial Court and against the said order, the petitioner has preferred Criminal Revision No.775/2023.

Since, the petitioner has already filed criminal revision No.775/2023 which is pending before this Court,
therefore, the same relief cannot be considered in the present petition.

4 . In the next relief i.e 7 (d), the petitioner has sought a direction to the Bar Council of Madhya Pradesh for cancellation of license of the respondent No.4, who is said to be an Advocate who was representing the petitioner, is registered as an advocate under the Advocates, Act, therefore, the remedy for seeking cancellation of license is under the Advocate, Act and not in the writ petition.
Hence, the relief claimed in clause 7(d) also cannot be considered in the present petition.
5 . By interim relief the petitioner has sought relief for summoning of certain documents under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Counsel for the State raises objection that the interim relief cannot be different and beyond the main relief.
Considering the fact that the petitioner is not an Advocate and is representing his own case, this Court do not accept the said technical objection of the counsel for the respondent.
This Court treats the interim relief as one of the main relief.

The petitioner is demanding following four documents from the respondents:-

a) Copy of the FIR.
b) Statement of witnesses under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
c) Statement of witnesses under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
d) The relevant documents relating to establish the charges.
6 . The present petition is entertained only for the relief of summoning the documents and not for the other reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
7. Counsel for the State submits that the aforesaid documents have already been supplied to the petitioner and he refers various Court orders to prove the said facts.
However, he submits that the respondents will supply another set of those documents to the petitioner before this Court on the next date.
8. On the next date, counsel for the State will make available the aforesaid documents as mentioned above.
9.At the request of counsel for the parties, list the matter on 20/7/2023.
2. In compliance to the said order the learned Public Prosecutor supplied all the documents which were part of the charge-sheet, on 20/7/2023 to the petitioner before this Court.
Thereafter, the petitioner filed two applications.
3. First, I.A No.5558/2023 which is an application for recall of the order dated 14/7/2023.
4. From going through the said application and after hearing learned counsel for the prosecutor, I do not find any case for recall of the order dated 14/7/2023.
The said order was passed after hearing the petitioner in the open Court who was present in person.
5. Accordingly, I.A. No.5558/2023 is dismissed.

6. Another application has been filed i.e I.A. No.5532/2023, which is an application under Section 340 of Cr.P.C for initiation of proceedings under Section 195 of Cr.P.C for offences under Sections 166, 166A, 191, 192, 193, 195, 196, 199, 200, 202, 203, 204, 209, 211, 212 and 120B of IPC against the public prosecutor who appeared in the case in High Court namely Shri Mukesh Parwal, Public Prosecutor and Shri Arvind Singh Tomar, OIC of the case alleging that they have supplied false and fabricated documents to the petitioner.
7. Counsel for the respondents submitted that the documents as directed by this Court have been supplied to the petitioner and they are part of the charge-sheet.
On the basis of the said documents charge has also been framed by the Trial Court and petitioner has filed Revision before this Court which has also been dismissed.
The allegations are false and concocted.
The petitioner is filing repeated same applications before the Trial Court.

sentences.text: The contention of the petitioner is that since his name is not in the FIR, therefore, the criminal case could not be registered against him.
This contention of the petitioner could not accepted.

Counsel for the respondent pointed out that the petitioner has been made accused on the basis of the memorandum recorded under Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act and he is facing criminal case of Crime No.09/2016, registered at Police Station Crime Branch, Indore for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120 B of IPC.
He further submits that it is established law that FIR is not an encyclopaedia.

9. Considering the aforesaid submissions, I find no case is made out for initiation of proceedings under Section 195 of Cr.P.C as the documents which are part of the charge-sheet has been supplied to the petitioner before this Court.
10. Accordingly, I.A. No.5532/2023 is dismissed.

11. At this stage, the petitioner prays that he will not get justice before this Court as previously his petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C was dismissed and requested to list the matter before another Bench.

He also stated that he has filed a writ petition at Principal Bench of this Court at Jabalpur,
M.P. against those judges who have passed the order against him impleading them party by name.
The prayer of the petitioner to transfer the case to other judge is rejected.
12. In view of the aforesaid, I do not find any case for recusing myself from the case only on this ground that because this Court has previously passed an adverse order against the petitioner.
13. As a consequence, the present writ petition stands dismissed.
CC as per rules.
(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE Pramod Ashok vs Shri Kailah Chandra Patidar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198199625/
